claims: The Butler Cabin is at Augusta National Golf Club.
The Butler Cabin was built in 1964.
The Butler Cabin is the site of the Masters Tournament’s Green Jacket ceremony.
The Butler Cabin is the site of television interviews.
The Butler Cabin is located near the 10th tee.
The Butler Cabin is where the winner receives the jacket from the previous year’s champion and CBS broadcaster Jim Nantz.
The winner is presented with the jacket on the 18th green.
The official presentation takes place inside the Butler Cabin.
Since 1965, the Butler Cabin has served as the final broadcasting hub for CBS.
The Butler Cabin has a rustic interior.
The Butler Cabin has a fireplace.
The Butler Cabin has a portrait of Bobby Jones.
The winner is interviewed in the Butler Cabin following the final round.
The low amateur is interviewed in the Butler Cabin following the final round.
Other top contenders are interviewed in the Butler Cabin following the final round.
The Butler Cabin was named after Thomas Butler.
Thomas Butler was a former member of Augusta National Golf Club.
The Butler Cabin serves as lodging for members and their guests when not in use for the tournament.
The Butler Cabin was first used for interviews in 1965.
Jack Nicklaus won his second Masters in 1965.
Jack Nicklaus and Tiger Woods hold the record for the most appearances at five each.
